title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages: X is an oriented topological or Riemann surface and x a point of it. S_x is the circle of tangent directions at x. D_x^* is a punctured disc neighbourhood of x. T_x = T_{X,x} is the rank-one Z-module of orientations at x, canonically pi_1 of both S_x and D_x^*. A_x is an ordered set of 'sectors': contractible arcs A of S_x, each with a corresponding angular sector E_p(A) in D_x^*.

We choose universal covers S~_x of S_x and D_x^{*~} of D_x^*. For each A, two sets are T_x-torsors: the sections S~_x(A) of the universal cover over A, and D_x^{*~}(E_p(A)). So is H(A) = Isom_{T_x}(S~_x(A), D_x^{*~}(E_p(A))). An inclusion A ⊂ A' gives restriction isomorphisms, hence a functor H: A_x -> Tors(T_x). This factors through the groupoid envelope Gr(A_x), obtained by inverting all arrows.

This page:
(103)-(105): Gr(A_x) is a connected 'T_x-groupoid'. Precisely, the functor A |-> S~_{x,A} (the universal cover of S_x pointed or rigidified by the sector A) factors through an equivalence Gr(A_x) ≃ Rev.univ.(S_x), the groupoid of universal coverings of S_x. So Hom_{Gr}(A,A') = Isom(S~_{x,A}, S~_{x,A'}), a T_x-torsor.

Claim: Gr(H) is essentially constant, i.e. it induces the zero homomorphism T_x -> T_x on pi_1. Equivalently, the H(A) are linked by a transitive system of isomorphisms compatible with (100).

One may therefore define the common value H(S~_x, D~_x^*). It depends only on the choice of the two universal covers and comes with compatible isomorphisms i_A: H(A) ≃ H(S~_x, D~_x^*), as in (106)-(107).

The next page proves this via the two equivalences F, G from Gr(A_x) to the covering categories of S_x and D_x^*, and functorial Isom descriptions. Behind it is a general lemma on connected T-groupoids.

Purpose: a canonical comparison between the universal cover of the punctured disc and that of the circle of tangent directions at x. This is a topological 'tangential base point' / boundary-circle identification, needed in the Longue Marche to attach base points at punctures (blown-up boundary circles) for the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim holds because a loop in Gr(A_x) acts on both torsors S~_x(A) and D~(E_p(A)) by the same element of T_x. This needs E_p to be orientation-compatible, which is implicit. Its action on the Isom-torsor H(A) is therefore trivial.
Minor: 'Rev univ(S_x)' on line (103) should be read as a category of (rigidified) universal coverings. The notation S~_{x,A} vs S~_x(A) is used loosely.

ideas.what: Groupoid envelope of the poset of sectors is equivalent to the groupoid of universal coverings of the circle (a connected groupoid with pi_1 = T_x)
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of a poset / Quillen–Segal: the nerve of an open-cover poset models the homotopy type
ideas.where_published: Similar ideas in SGA1 and Pursuing Stacks; this precise statement unpublished

ideas.what: Canonical torsor H(S~_x, D~_x^*) identifying the universal cover of the punctured disc with that of the circle of tangent directions
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / boundary-circle (real blow-up) base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, P^1 minus three points), Ihara, Nakamura; topological version via real oriented blow-up (A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama)
ideas.where_published: The Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse discuss base points at the boundary/punctures in spirit; this explicit construction is unpublished

ideas.what: Essential constancy criterion: a functor from a connected T-groupoid to Tors(T) inducing zero on pi_1 gives a transitive system and a well-defined 'common value'
ideas.modern_name: Local system with trivial monodromy / limit of a constant diagram over a groupoid

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine topological construction: canonical identification of the universal covers of the punctured disc and of the tangent circle, i.e. a topological tangential base point. It is consistent with known Longue Marche themes. The idea of tangential base points is well established in the literature (Deligne, Ihara), so nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'est un Teichmüller groupoïde' should read 'est un T_x-groupoïde' ('un Tx-' at line end, then 'groupoïde'). This is confirmed by 'T-groupoïdes connexes' on the next page.
'il définit sur ces π_1 l'homomorphisme T_x → T_x [?]' should read 'il définit sur les π_1 l'homomorphisme nul T_x →(0) T_x'. The arrow is decorated with 0.
'le "colimite [?] commune"' is likely 'la "valeur commune"' of the H(A).
'structure définie par des isom. de Teichmüller [?]' should read 'des isom. de T_x-torseurs' ('Tx-torseurs' written at line end).
Lines 2-3 should probably read 'On sait que Gr(A_x) est un T_x-groupoïde, de façon précise le foncteur'.
In (103) the target is 'Rev univ(S_x)' with value S~_{x,A}, written over the crossed-out 'Rev univ(S,A)'.
